title: charlesfoster/wasteline pipeline parameters
description: Wastewater SARS-CoV-2 lineage abundance pipeline (Illumina amplicon, Freyja)

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the samplesheet CSV; its columns depend on `--mode`. Required for `full`.
input.help_text: Path to a comma-separated samplesheet. Columns depend on `--mode`: `full` sample,fastq_1,fastq_2; `demix` sample,variants,depths; `aggregate` sample,demix. All modes accept optional sample_type,collection_date,site (fastp_json too for `demix`). Required by `--mode full`; optional for `demix` (alternative: `--previous_results`) and `aggregate` (alternatives: `--demix_dir`, `--previous_results`); not used by `report` and `update_db`. `sample` may only contain letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` and is never rewritten. `sample_type` is `sample` (default) or `negative`; `collection_date` is ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. The columns are validated against assets/schema_input.json (full), assets/schema_input_demix.json or assets/schema_input_aggregate.json. See docs/usage.md.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved.
outdir.help_text: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

mode.help_text: `full`: FASTQ to aggregated Freyja results. `demix`: re-run `freyja demix` (e.g. with newer barcodes) on existing variants/depths files, then aggregate. `aggregate`: aggregate existing `.demix` files only. `report`: rebuild the HTML report of a previous run (`--results_dir`, written to a different `--outdir`). `update_db`: download the latest Freyja data into `--db_dir` and exit.

previous_results.description: Modes `demix`/`aggregate`: results directory (or several, comma-separated) of an earlier run.
previous_results.help_text: Modes `demix`/`aggregate`: results directory (or several, comma-separated) of an earlier run, from wasteline or from the legacy Snakemake pipeline. Never modified. Both layouts are detected per sample: `samples/<sample>/freyja/` (wasteline) and `<sample>/freyja/` (Snakemake). Gzipped legacy variants files are handled. Alternative to `--input`; discovery uses `bin/make_samplesheet.py --from-results`, and `sample_type`, `collection_date` and `site` are carried over from the results' `summary/samplesheet.csv` when present (otherwise IDs matching `NEG_|NC_` are negative controls).

demix_dir.description: Mode `aggregate`: directory searched recursively for `*.demix` files.
demix_dir.help_text: Mode `aggregate`: directory searched (recursively) for `*.demix` files. The sample ID is the file name without `.demix`. Alternative to `--input`. IDs matching `NEG_|NC_` are treated as negative controls.

results_dir.description: Mode `report`: results directory of a previous run to re-render the report from.
results_dir.help_text: Mode `report`: results directory of a previous run. Needs `pipeline_info/run_info.json`; `summary/report_data.json` is reused when present, otherwise rebuilt from the other files in `summary/`. `--outdir` must differ from it.

include_negatives_in_aggregate.description: Include negative controls (`sample_type=negative`) in `freyja aggregate` and the plots.
include_negatives_in_aggregate.help_text: Negative controls that pass the coverage gate are always demixed and listed in `demix_status.tsv`, but by default they are kept out of the aggregate and plots (PLAN D8).

include_low_confidence.description: Keep `low_confidence` samples in the time series, growth rates, dashboard and site aggregation.
include_low_confidence.help_text: Samples between `--demix_floor_coverage` and `--min_genome_coverage_for_demix` are demixed and flagged `low_confidence` (PLAN D18). They appear in `freyja_aggregated.tsv`, the lineage summary and the report, but by default are left out of the time-based analyses and site aggregation. Mode `aggregate` with given `.demix` files treats every sample as `ok` (no coverage information), so this has no effect there.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

library_protocol_options.title: Library protocol
library_protocol_options.description: How the reads were made: PCR amplicons (primer-trimmed) or probe capture (not trimmed).

protocol.description: Library protocol: `amplicon` (tiled PCR amplicons, primer-trimmed) or `capture` (probe capture).
protocol.help_text: Library protocol. `amplicon` (default): tiled PCR amplicons, reads are primer-trimmed. `capture`: probe-capture libraries (e.g. Twist): no primer trimming, no amplicon-dropout analysis, PCR duplicates are marked. With `capture`, `--primer_scheme` and `--primer_bed` are ignored (with a warning). The protocol is recorded in run_info.json and shown in the report header.

skip_primer_trimming.description: Do not primer-trim (`ivar trim`). For reads that are already trimmed. Implied by `--protocol capture`. Amplicon-level QC is off too: `--primer_scheme`/`--primer_bed` are ignored.

duplicates.description: PCR-duplicate handling after alignment. `mark`: flag duplicates (`samtools markdup`); Freyja's pileup then ignores them. `none`: leave them. `auto`: `mark` for `--protocol capture`, `none` for `amplicon`.
duplicates.help_text: Duplicates are flagged, never removed. Not used by modes without reads (`demix`, `aggregate`).

reference_and_primer_options.title: Reference and primer options
reference_and_primer_options.description: Reference genome and amplicon primer scheme.

fasta.description: Path to the reference FASTA. Default: the bundled reference of the pathogen (conf/pathogens/*.config); required for pathogens without one.
fasta.help_text: The BWA index is built from this file once per run. For a pathogen other than SARS-CoV-2, MEASLESgenome, MPX, RSVa, RSVb and the influenza pathogens this must be the reference.fasta that the Freyja barcodes were built on (the pathogen's folder in the Freyja-barcodes repository). A FASTA with several sequences (a segmented genome, or a genome plus other targets) is accepted only together with `--freyja_contig <name of the sequence Freyja demixes>` (or with `--whole_genome` for the bundled influenza references); every sequence then gets depth QC, variant calls and a consensus genome.

gff.description: Path to the reference annotation (GFF3). Default: the bundled annotation (SARS-CoV-2, MPX, RSVa, RSVb, influenza). Optional for the other pathogens; `--annotate_variants` needs it.

whole_genome.description: Influenza H1N1, H3N2, H5Nx and H5Nx-cattle: map the reads to all eight segments (bundled `<HA accession>_wg.fasta`) instead of the HA segment only.
whole_genome.help_text: Freyja still demixes the HA segment only (its barcodes cover nothing else); the other seven segments get depth QC, variant calls and a consensus genome, and the report shows a per-segment coverage table. B/Victoria (FLU-B-VIC) has no whole-genome reference yet. For any other multi-sequence reference give `--fasta` and `--freyja_contig` instead. See docs/other_pathogens.md.

primer_scheme.description: Name of an amplicon primer scheme (bundled, or `<name>.bed` in `--primer_scheme_dir`).
primer_scheme.help_text: Name of an amplicon primer scheme: bundled for the pathogen (assets/primer_schemes/) or a `<name>.bed` in `--primer_scheme_dir`. Default: `qiagenv1` for SARS-CoV-2 in mode `full`; other pathogens have no default. SARS-CoV-2: midnight, midnightv2, articv3, articv4.1, articv5.3.2, eden, swift, qiagenv1, xgen. MEASLESgenome: artic-measles-v1.0.0. MPX: bccdc-mpox-v2.3.0, yale-mpox-2000-v1.0.0-lifted, artic-inrb-mpox-2500-v1.0.0-cladeiib. RSVa: rsva-rsv-pipeline, rsva-1000-v1.0.0-lifted. RSVb: rsvb-rsv-pipeline, rsvb-1000-v1.0.0-lifted. A name found in `--primer_scheme_dir` wins over a bundled one. An unknown name stops the run at start-up and lists the names available for the pathogen. Ignored if `--primer_bed` is given. The `swift` scheme implies `--ivar_offset 5`. In mode `demix` the scheme of the old results is unknown, so per-amplicon coverage is only computed when `--primer_scheme` or `--primer_bed` is given explicitly.

primer_scheme_dir.description: Directory of your own primer schemes: `<name>.bed` files, usable by name in `--primer_scheme` and in the samplesheet `primer_scheme` column.
primer_scheme_dir.help_text: Each BED needs the reference's contig name in column 1 (checked at start-up for the schemes that are used) and primalscheme-style primer names (`<scheme>_<n>_LEFT_<alt>` / `_RIGHT_<alt>`) so that amplicons can be paired. A name that is also bundled for the pathogen uses your file, with a warning. See docs/usage.md, "Using your own primer scheme".

primer_bed.help_text: The contig name must match the reference FASTA. With a custom BED the ivar offset defaults to 0; set `--ivar_offset` if needed.

ivar_offset.description: `ivar trim -x` primer position offset. Default: 5 for the bundled `swift` scheme, otherwise 0.

pathogen.description: Freyja `--pathogen` name. Default: SARS-CoV-2 (bundled reference, primer schemes, lineage groups).
pathogen.help_text: Freyja `--pathogen` name. Default: SARS-CoV-2 (bundled reference, annotation, primer schemes and lineage groups). MEASLESgenome, MPX, RSVa, RSVb and the five influenza pathogens (H1N1, H3N2, FLU-B-VIC, H5Nx, H5Nx-cattle; HA segment only) have a bundled reference; every other single-contig pathogen needs `--fasta`. Passed to every Freyja call. The per-pathogen defaults (reference, annotation) come from conf/pathogens/<profile>.config. Without `--fasta` and `--primer_bed` only SARS-CoV-2 runs out of the box; pass `--fasta` = the reference.fasta that the pathogen's Freyja barcodes were built on (a different one gives silently wrong results), `--primer_bed` (or `--protocol capture`), and `--lineage_groups` if you want the lineage-group summary. Freyja's influenza barcodes (H5Nx, H5Nx-cattle, H1N1, H3N2, FLU-B-VIC) cover the HA segment only: the bundled reference is the HA sequence, one run per subtype, reads of the other segments do not map. MTB (4.4 Mb) is accepted by Freyja but stops here with an explanation. See docs/other_pathogens.md.
pathogen.errorMessage: --pathogen must be one of the Freyja pathogens: SARS-CoV-2, MPX, H5Nx, H5Nx-cattle, H1N1, H3N2, FLU-B-VIC, MEASLESgenome, RSVa, RSVb, DENV1, DENV2, DENV3, DENV4, MTB (MTB is not supported, see docs/other_pathogens.md).

lineage_groups_bundled.description: Set by conf/pathogens/*.config, not for users: the pathogen's bundled lineage groups file (none = the lineage-group summary is off unless `--lineage_groups` is given).

freyja_container_pathogen.description: Set by conf/pathogens/*.config, not for users: the pathogen whose data the pinned Freyja container bundles (`--barcodes container`); its datasets live in <db_dir>/freyja, those of other pathogens in <db_dir>/freyja_<pathogen>.

primer_schemes_bundled.description: Set by conf/pathogens/*.config, not for users: the directory of the pathogen's bundled `<name>.bed` primer schemes (none = no bundled scheme; use `--primer_bed`, `--primer_scheme_dir` or `--protocol capture`).

primer_scheme_default.description: Set by conf/pathogens/*.config, not for users: the bundled scheme used in mode `full` when no scheme or BED is given (SARS-CoV-2: `qiagenv1`; none for other pathogens, which then stop with a message).

freyja_contig.description: The name of the reference sequence Freyja demixes when `--fasta` has several (the first word of its FASTA header). Set by conf/pathogens/*.config with `--whole_genome`; give it yourself with a custom multi-sequence `--fasta`. Null for a single-sequence reference.

panel_options.title: Panel options
panel_options.description: Several targets (pathogens) in one run. In development: panel runs are not available in this build yet.

panel.description: Analyse several targets in one run: a built-in panel name (`rsv`, `flu`) or a panel CSV.
panel.help_text: Analyse several targets in one run: a built-in panel name (`rsv`: RSVa, RSVb; `flu`: H1N1, H3N2, H5Nx, FLU-B-VIC) or the path to a panel CSV. A panel CSV has a `target` column naming rows of assets/panels/registry.csv (the Freyja pathogens with barcodes) and optional columns that override a registry column of that target (for example `primer_scheme`). Each sample is typed against the panel and every detected target is analysed with its own reference and barcodes. Cannot be combined with `--pathogen`, `--fasta`, `--gff`, `--freyja_contig` or `--whole_genome`. See docs/usage.md (Panels).

targets.description: Comma-separated targets of the results of a panel run that modes `demix`, `aggregate` and `report` should use (default: all targets).
targets.help_text: For example `--targets RSVa,RSVb`. Names are those of the panel's targets (assets/panels/registry.csv). Not used by `--mode full`, which analyses every target of the panel.

panel_min_fragments.description: A target is detected in a sample only with at least this many read fragments assigned to it.
panel_min_fragments.help_text: Typing thresholds are not calibrated on real data yet. A target with some fragments that misses a threshold is reported as `trace` (listed in summary/targets.tsv, not analysed).

panel_min_breadth_pct.description: A target is detected only if at least this % of its marker sequence is covered by its fragments.

panel_family_share_pct.description: Within a family (for example RSV, or influenza A) a target that is not the top one is detected only with at least this % of the family's fragments.
panel_family_share_pct.help_text: Guards against cross-mapping between close relatives (RSVa and RSVb) inflating a minor target.

panel_mapq.description: A read fragment is assigned to a target only if all its mapped reads have at least this mapping quality on the target's contigs.

read_trimming_and_bam_options.title: Read trimming and BAM options
read_trimming_and_bam_options.description: fastp settings (defaults reproduce the Snakemake pipeline) and what to keep.

fastp_length_required.description: fastp `--length_required` (reads shorter than this are discarded).

save_bam.description: Publish the primer-trimmed, sorted BAM and index.

freyja_options.title: Freyja options
freyja_options.description: Freyja barcode data and analysis settings.

barcodes.description: Freyja barcode dataset: `latest`, `container`, a version, or a dataset directory / file.
barcodes.help_text: Freyja barcode dataset: `latest`, `container`, a version (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `MM_DD_YYYY-HH-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM`), or a dataset directory / `.csv` / `.feather` file. `latest` runs `freyja update` and stores the dataset in `--db_dir/freyja/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM>/`. `container` uses the snapshot bundled in the pinned Freyja container (offline). A version resolves a dataset previously stored in `--db_dir` (a bare date picks the newest that day) and errors if none exists. A path is used verbatim (version recorded as `custom`). The dataset is resolved once so every sample uses the same data; the version and checksums are recorded in `pipeline_info/run_info.json` and `summary/barcode_version.json`.

db_dir.description: Writable directory for downloaded Freyja datasets. Default: `~/.wasteline/db`.

freyja_varthresh.help_text: Freyja's own default (0.0, keep everything). The old Snakemake pipeline used 0.25; this pipeline deliberately does not.

freyja_eps.description: `freyja demix --eps`: minimum abundance reported per lineage.

freyja_covcut.description: `freyja demix --covcut`: depth that counts a site as covered (also used for the coverage gate).

freyja_depthcutoff.description: `freyja demix --depthcutoff`: exclude sites below this depth and group identical barcodes (0 = off).

freyja_autoadapt.description: `freyja demix --autoadapt`: set the adaptive penalty from the sample's error profile.

freyja_solver.description: `freyja demix --solver`: solver for the abundance estimate.

compare_barcodes.description: A second Freyja dataset (same forms as `--barcodes`): every sample is demixed again with it and `summary/barcode_compare.tsv` lists the abundance changes. Modes `full` and `demix`.
compare_barcodes.help_text: Recorded as `freyja_data_compare` in run_info.json. A sample whose second demix fails is flagged, never fatal. Default: off.

freyja_boot.description: Run `freyja boot` per demixed sample: bootstrap 95% intervals per lineage.
freyja_boot.help_text: Run `freyja boot` per demixed sample: bootstrap 95% intervals (2.5/97.5 percentiles) per lineage in `summary/freyja_boot_summary.tsv`.

freyja_boot_seed.description: Bootstrap seed (`freyja boot --bootseed`); fixed, so reruns give identical intervals.

freyja_plot_mincov.description: Minimum genome coverage (%) for a sample to appear in `freyja_plot.pdf` (`freyja plot --mincov`), the time series, the growth rates and the dashboard. Default: follow the pipeline, i.e. `--min_genome_coverage_for_demix` (50), or with `--include_low_confidence` the floor `--demix_floor_coverage` (25).
freyja_plot_mincov.help_text: Not set = every sample that was demixed and is meant to be analysed appears. Freyja keeps a sample only when its coverage is strictly above this value. An explicit value always wins (the previous fixed default was 60, which hid samples between 50 and 60 %).

freyja_plot_config.description: Freyja plot config (YAML) passed as `--config` to `freyja plot`, `freyja dash` and `freyja relgrowthrate`: your own colours and custom lineage groups.
freyja_plot_config.help_text: Keys: `VOC` (colours of the groups in the stacked-bar plot `freyja_plot.pdf`) and `Lineages` (groups and colours of the lineage-level views, the dashboard and the growth rates). The HTML report keeps its own palette. See docs/usage.md (Plot colours and lineage groups).

freyja_plot_interval.description: Interval of the time-aware plot (`freyja plot --times`, drawn when samples have a `collection_date`): month (`MS`), week (`W`) or day (`D`).

freyja_plot_windowsize.description: Rolling-average window (days) of the daily (`D`) time-aware plot.

min_genome_coverage_for_demix.description: High-confidence threshold: % of the genome at depth >= `--freyja_covcut` needed to demix.
min_genome_coverage_for_demix.help_text: High-confidence threshold: samples with less than this % of the genome at depth >= `--freyja_covcut` are flagged `low_confidence` (from `--demix_floor_coverage` up) or not demixed (status `skipped_low_coverage`). Default 50, from real wastewater data (28 QIAseq samples: the median sample has only 58 % of the genome at >= 10x, mostly because of amplicon dropout, not too few reads). Below this an abundance estimate rests on too little of the lineage-defining sites to trust. Samples below `--demix_floor_coverage` are skipped, listed in `summary/demix_status.tsv` and excluded from the aggregate. Freyja's own plot hides samples below `--freyja_plot_mincov` (60).

demix_floor_coverage.description: Floor of the low-confidence band: below this % of the genome a sample is not demixed.
demix_floor_coverage.help_text: Floor of the low-confidence band: samples with at least this % of the genome at depth >= `--freyja_covcut` but below `--min_genome_coverage_for_demix` are demixed and flagged `low_confidence`. Default 25 (PLAN D18): in real QIAseq wastewater data 10 of 28 samples sit at 25-50 % and half of those have a mean depth >= 200x (amplicon dropout, not read shortage), so skipping them threw away usable signal. Below the floor a sample is skipped (`skipped_low_coverage`). Set 0, or a value at or above `--min_genome_coverage_for_demix`, to switch the band off (the behaviour before D18). Low-confidence samples are left out of the time series, growth rates, dashboard and site aggregation unless `--include_low_confidence true`.

coverage_qc_options.title: Coverage QC and negative controls
coverage_qc_options.description: Per-sample coverage QC from the Freyja depths file (PLAN D7) and negative-control assessment (PLAN D8).

amplicon_min_depth.description: An amplicon is dropped when its mean depth is below this.

qc_min_depth.description: Depth used for the PASS/WARN/FAIL coverage test.

qc_pass_min_pct.description: PASS needs at least this % of the genome at `--qc_min_depth`.
qc_pass_min_pct.help_text: PASS needs at least this % of the genome at `qc_min_depth`. Default 60 (it was 80 in the clinical pipeline: real wastewater samples rarely reach it).

qc_fail_below_pct.description: FAIL below this % of the genome at `--qc_min_depth`; between this and PASS is WARN.
qc_fail_below_pct.help_text: FAIL below this % of the genome at `qc_min_depth`. Default 30; between this and `--qc_pass_min_pct` is WARN (`low_coverage`).

qc_max_dropped_amplicons.description: WARN (`amplicon_dropout`) when more amplicons than this dropped. Raise it for schemes with many amplicons (e.g. 10 for 99-amplicon ARTIC).

ntc_max_mapped_reads.description: A negative control FAILs (`ntc_reads`) above this many mapped reads.

ntc_max_genome_coverage_pct.description: A negative control FAILs above this % of the genome at >= 1x.

consensus_options.title: Consensus genomes
consensus_options.description: Per-sample consensus built from the Freyja variants TSV and depths file (PLAN 5.11). Negative controls get none.

skip_consensus.description: Skip the consensus chain and the consensus summaries.

consensus_min_depth.description: Positions below this depth are masked (N); also used for `pct_genome_ge_min_depth`.

consensus_freq.description: SNV ALT_FREQ needed to apply the alternative allele.

indel_freq.description: Indel ALT_FREQ needed to apply it.

consensus_min_depth_variants.description: Minimum TOTAL_DP at a variant (not the mask depth `consensus_min_depth`).

consensus_iupac.description: Write IUPAC codes for ambiguous SNVs; false leaves the reference base.

consensus_iupac_min_af.description: SNV ALT_FREQ must be above this (and below `consensus_freq`) for an IUPAC code.

consensus_iupac_min_alt_reads.description: ALT_DP needed for an IUPAC code.

qc_checks_options.title: QC checks
qc_checks_options.description: Checks beyond coverage: is the primer scheme right, what do dropped amplicons hide, which mutations does the lineage mixture not explain.

primer_scheme_check.description: Check that the primer scheme matches the reads (amplicon protocol with primer trimming, mode `full`).
primer_scheme_check.help_text: Counts mapped reads whose 5' end sits at a primer 5' end of each bundled scheme and compares the declared scheme with the others (enrichment over chance). Result `ok`, `mismatch` or `uninformative` in `qc_summary.tsv`; a mismatch is a WARN (`primer_scheme_mismatch`). Libraries whose reads are not primer-anchored (e.g. tagmentation) give `uninformative`.

primer_check_min_enrichment.description: Enrichment of read starts at primers (times chance) needed for the declared scheme to count as matching.

primer_check_min_hit_fraction.description: Fraction of reads that must start within the window of a primer 5' end for a scheme to count as matching (0 disables). Stops sparse schemes whose enrichment ratio is inflated by a tiny window set.

primer_check_window.description: Window (bp) around a primer 5' end that counts as `at the primer`.

qc_min_primer_trimmed_pct.description: WARN (`low_primer_trimming`) when the % of mapped reads that `ivar trim` primer-trimmed is below this. 0 disables.
qc_min_primer_trimmed_pct.help_text: Only meaningful for protocols whose reads start at primer sites; calibrate on your own good runs (a value around half the lowest good run).

dropout_impact.description: Report which lineage-informative sites dropped amplicons hide (`summary/dropout_impact.tsv`). Needs an amplicon table (amplicon protocol).

dropout_min_abundance.description: A lineage counts as detected at this abundance when assessing dropout impact (it is then listed and its defining sites are counted).

dropout_min_affect_abundance.description: Minimum abundance of a detected lineage for its DEFINING sites (mutations that separate it from its parent) in a dropped amplicon to raise the dropout flag (`affects_detected_lineage`).

unexplained_mutations.description: Find frequent mutations the demixed lineages do not predict (`summary/unexplained_mutations.tsv`; modes `full` and `demix`).
unexplained_mutations.help_text: A hint of a novel or missing lineage, not a variant caller: observed frequency minus the frequency expected from the lineage mixture, with a binomial guard against depth noise.

unexplained_min_freq.description: Minimum observed frequency of the mutation.

unexplained_min_depth.description: Minimum total depth at the position.

unexplained_min_alt_depth.description: Minimum number of reads supporting the mutation.

unexplained_min_recurrence.description: The same mutation unexplained in at least this many samples is flagged `recurrent`.

unexplained_max_pvalue.description: Binomial guard against depth noise (Bonferroni-style over the genome); 1 disables it.

surveillance_options.title: Surveillance outputs
surveillance_options.description: Time-series outputs from the collection dates (and optional viral load) in the samplesheet.

timeseries.description: Write `summary/freyja_timeseries.tsv` (+ `_lineages.tsv`) when at least two distinct collection dates exist.

timeseries_min_abundance.description: Drop site-date lineage groups below this mean abundance.

freyja_growth.description: Estimate relative growth rates of lineages with `freyja relgrowthrate`.
freyja_growth.help_text: Estimate relative growth rates of lineages with `freyja relgrowthrate` (`summary/freyja_growth_rates.csv`). Needs at least `--freyja_growth_min_dates` distinct dates spanning at least `--freyja_growth_min_span_days` days within the last `--freyja_growth_days` days; otherwise `summary/freyja_growth_rates.failed.txt` says why. A failure never fails the run.

freyja_growth_days.description: Window (days back from the latest date) used for the fit.

freyja_growth_serial_interval.description: Serial interval (days): the advantage is `exp(serial_interval * r) - 1`.

freyja_growth_grthresh.description: Only lineages with a mean abundance above this over the window get a rate.

freyja_growth_min_abundance.description: Per-sample abundance below which a lineage is lumped into `Other`.

freyja_growth_min_dates.description: Fewer distinct dates in the window than this: no growth rates (failure note).

freyja_growth_min_span_days.description: The dates must span at least this many days.

freyja_growth_scale_by_viral_load.description: Weight by `viral_load` (`freyja relgrowthrate --scale_by_viral_load`); samples without a load are dropped from the fit.

freyja_dash.help_text: Opt-in extra. The HTML embeds Plotly but loads Bootstrap styling and a logo from the internet when opened; the pipeline's own `report.html` stays offline.

freyja_dash_intro.default: Lineage prevalence over time from wasteline.

alignment_storage_options.title: Alignment and storage
alignment_storage_options.description: Which aligner maps the reads and in which format the alignments are kept.

aligner.description: Read aligner. `bwa` (bwa mem) is the default and validated choice; `minibwa` is experimental.
aligner.help_text: minibwa is a young successor of bwa-mem; its alignments are not identical to bwa mem's. Compare with `tests/compare_aligners.sh` before relying on it; see docs/aligner_evaluation.md.

bam_format.help_text: `cram` publishes a reference-based CRAM and its `.crai` instead of the BAM and `.bai` (about a third of the size). Reading a CRAM needs the same reference FASTA (`samtools view --reference ref.fa`). Freyja and all QC steps still use the BAM, which stays in the work directory.

lineage_groups_and_sites_options.title: Lineage groups and site aggregation
lineage_groups_and_sites_options.description: User-defined lineage groups per sample (on by default, with the bundled list `assets/lineage_groups.csv`), and result-level aggregation of sites into groups of sites (off unless a CSV is given).

lineage_summary.description: Write the per-sample table of lineage groups (`summary/lineage_summary.csv`, plus the groups file used and a list of lineages in no group). `--lineage_summary false` turns it off.
lineage_summary.help_text: Needs a Freyja dataset with lineages.yml (not a bare barcodes .csv/.feather); with such a dataset the summary is skipped with one warning.

lineage_groups.description: CSV that defines the lineage groups. Default: the bundled `assets/lineage_groups.csv` (SARS-CoV-2).
lineage_groups.help_text: CSV that defines the lineage groups (columns `group`, `include`, optional `exclude`, `in_total`). Default: the bundled `assets/lineage_groups.csv` (SARS-CoV-2 only; other pathogens have the summary off unless this is given). A copy of the file used is published as `summary/lineage_groups_used.csv`. One row per output column; patterns such as `JN.1*` (the lineage and all its descendants), `NB.1.8.1` (exactly that lineage) and `RECOMBINANT*`. Start from the bundled file (or a previous run's `lineage_groups_used.csv`), edit it in Excel and save as CSV UTF-8. Format errors stop the run within minutes; unknown lineages are warnings. See docs/usage.md (Lineage groups).

lineage_major_threshold.description: Abundance at or above which a lineage is listed as `major` in `lineage_summary.csv` (exactly this value counts as major).

lineage_min_abundance.description: Lineages below this abundance are not listed (the group sums still include them).

lineage_summary_zeros.description: How a group with no abundance is written in `lineage_summary.csv`: an empty cell or `0.000000`.

lineage_summary_xlsx.description: Also write `summary/lineage_summary.xlsx`: a formatted Excel workbook of the lineage summary (numbers as numbers, frozen header, filter; the CSV is unchanged).

lineage_summary_xlsx_decimals.description: Decimals shown for abundances in the workbook (display only; the stored values are the CSV values).

site_aggregation.description: CSV that groups sites into aggregates; enables the site-aggregate summaries. Off when not set.
site_aggregation.help_text: CSV that groups sites into aggregates (columns `aggregate_name`, `site_name`, optional `weight`); enables `summary/site_aggregates_freyja.tsv` and `site_aggregates_meta.tsv`. Off when not set. Per-site Freyja results are combined by a weighted average of the RESULTS (reads are never pooled). Site names are matched to the samplesheet `site` column ignoring case and extra spaces. Format errors stop the run within minutes. See docs/usage.md (Site aggregation).

site_aggregation_period.description: Time step of the site aggregates: ISO `week` (Monday to Sunday) or `day`.

site_aggregation_weights.description: Weights of the sites in an aggregate: `viral_load` (the samplesheet column), `site_weight` (the `weight` column of the sites file), `equal`, or `auto` (the best basis available for every site of that week, recorded per row).

site_aggregation_min_sites.description: Omit aggregate-weeks with fewer contributing sites than this.

report_anonymize.description: Remove identifying strings from the report so it can be shared: `paths` or `full`.
report_anonymize.help_text: Remove identifying strings from `report_data.json` and `report.html` so the report can be shared: `paths` (file paths, user and host names), `full` (also sample IDs and site names, replaced by `S001`, `SITE1`, ...). `full` also writes the private mapping `summary/sample_id_map.csv`: keep it OUT of anything you share with the report. All other files in `summary/` (for example `qc_summary.tsv`) keep the real IDs. In mode `report` the report data are rebuilt from the summary files when this is not `none`.

mutations_of_interest.description: CSV with columns `name,mutation`; frequency and depth per sample are reported.
mutations_of_interest.help_text: CSV with columns `name,mutation` (e.g. `S:N501Y`, `A23063T`, `C75-`, `A14+C`); frequency and depth per sample go to `summary/mutations_of_interest.tsv`.

annotate_variants.description: Annotate called variants with their amino-acid consequences (`bcftools csq`).
annotate_variants.help_text: Annotate the called variants with their amino-acid consequences (`bcftools csq` with the GFF3): `samples/<s>/variants/<s>.annotated.tsv` and `summary/annotated_variants.tsv`.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help.description: Display the help message. Give a parameter name for its details: `--help <param>`.

help_full.description: Display the full help message: every parameter, advanced ones included.

show_hidden.description: Also show hidden parameters in `--help` (implied by `--help_full`).
show_hidden.help_text: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
